name: Vision-based robot alignment
summary: Limelight vision cameras and PID control help the robot align with scoring locations.
approach: Team 867 has used Limelight vision cameras together with PID control to automatically align our robot with scoring locations on the field. Rather than depending completely on a driver’s reaction time, the robot uses information from its camera to continuously calculate its position error and correct its movement.
future: Our Controls team wants to continue expanding computer vision and localization.

Future development includes experimenting with AI-based vision to better identify field geometry and corners, improving the robot’s understanding of its position, and potentially strengthening odometry and autonomous movement.
source: Packet p. 11; project year not given

name: Multi-stage elevator system
summary: A custom mechanism moves game pieces vertically across scoring heights.
challenge: One of our recent robots required the ability to move game pieces vertically across various scoring heights.
approach: Our solution was a custom elevator mechanism designed, manufactured, assembled, and tested by Team 867 students. Considerations: structural rigidity, motor selection, gear ratios, weight, stability, packaging, & software control.
Projects like this allow members to see how mechanical, electrical, software, and CAD decisions directly support each other.
source: Packet p. 11; robot name and year not supplied

name: Game piece collection
summary: Hoppers and intake mechanisms collect, retain, and move game pieces.
approach: Our robots have also incorporated systems such as hoppers and intake mechanisms designed to quickly collect, retain, and move game pieces through the robot. A successful mechanism rarely begins with the final design. We prototype, test, break, redesign and rebuild, and this is our signature process.
source: Packet p. 11; robot name and year not supplied

name: Still Water · Bucket Brigade
summary: An Archimedes screw moves water in the Bucket Brigade challenge.
challenge: This year, the JPL Invention Challenge was to move 8 liters of water from a reservoir into a bucket 16 feet away as fast as possible while satisfying many rules, such as no pumps allowed or no more than 2 liters of water can be travelling upwards at a single time.
approach: Its design featured an Archimedes screw.
results: At JPL, Still Water was able to achieve 1st place, moving the 8 liters in just 6.45 seconds.
2 out of our 3 Team 867 groups qualified for the Finals.
source: Wix Over the Years, October–December 2025; packet pp. 10, 13. User confirmed December 2025 in this conversation.
